questions.prompt: Which document gives a maker the exact sizes, materials, finish, and construction notes needed to produce a design?
options: Working drawing
Mood board
Colour collage
Attendance sheet
questions.correctAnswer: Working drawing
questions.explanation: A working drawing communicates the technical information required for accurate production.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the purpose of working drawings in product manufacture.

questions.prompt: Which line convention normally shows the centre of a hole or circular feature?
options: Chain thin centre line
Continuous thick outline
Freehand break line
Random shading line
questions.correctAnswer: Chain thin centre line
questions.explanation: Centre lines mark axes of symmetry and the centres of circular features.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise standard line types used in technical drawings.

questions.prompt: What does a tolerance on a dimension state?
options: The allowed variation from the stated size
The colour to use for rendering
The drawing paper brand
The number of sketches in a portfolio
questions.correctAnswer: The allowed variation from the stated size
questions.explanation: Tolerances define how much a size may vary while the part still functions as intended.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Define tolerance as an accepted size variation in production.

questions.prompt: Which view is used to show the true shape of an inclined surface in orthographic projection?
options: Auxiliary view
Title view
Freehand view
Parts-list view
questions.correctAnswer: Auxiliary view
questions.explanation: An auxiliary view is projected perpendicular to an inclined surface to show its true shape.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify auxiliary views as a method for showing true shapes.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a sectional view?
options: To reveal internal details by imagining a cut through an object
To remove all dimensions from a drawing
To show only the title block
To turn a drawing into a material list
questions.correctAnswer: To reveal internal details by imagining a cut through an object
questions.explanation: A sectional view exposes hidden internal features more clearly than many dashed hidden lines.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of sectional drawing in technical communication.

questions.prompt: In first-angle orthographic projection, where is the plan commonly placed relative to the front view?
options: Below the front view
Above the front view
Inside the title block
Only on a separate sheet
questions.correctAnswer: Below the front view
questions.explanation: In first-angle projection, views are placed opposite the viewing direction, so the plan is commonly below the front view.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall view placement in first-angle projection.

questions.prompt: Which pictorial drawing uses three axes that are equally inclined to represent width, height, and depth?
options: Isometric drawing
Bar chart
Sectional plan
Flow diagram
questions.correctAnswer: Isometric drawing
questions.explanation: Isometric drawing represents three dimensions on equally inclined axes.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify isometric drawing as a 3D representation method.

questions.prompt: Which rendering technique makes an object look more three-dimensional by showing light and dark areas?
options: Shading
Numbering pages
Erasing borders
Copying file names
questions.correctAnswer: Shading
questions.explanation: Shading shows tonal differences caused by light, helping the viewer understand form.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify shading as a method for communicating form.

questions.prompt: What is a surface development?
options: A flat pattern of surfaces before folding or forming
A final product photograph only
A list of unrelated colours
A hidden line inside a border
questions.correctAnswer: A flat pattern of surfaces before folding or forming
questions.explanation: Surface development lays out the true shapes of surfaces so material can be cut and formed.
questions.learningOutcome: Define surface development as a flat pattern for production.

questions.prompt: Which feature on a packaging net shows where the material should bend?
options: Fold line
Centre punch
Cutting oil
Vanishing point
questions.correctAnswer: Fold line
questions.explanation: Fold lines guide accurate bending so panels form the intended package shape.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify fold lines in package developments.

questions.prompt: What does CAD mean in Drawing & Design?
options: Computer-aided design
Class attendance diary
Colour and decoration
Cutting angle diagram
questions.correctAnswer: Computer-aided design
questions.explanation: CAD means using computer software to create, edit, store, and output design drawings.
questions.learningOutcome: Define CAD in a drawing and design context.

questions.prompt: Which CAD tool helps keep outlines, hidden lines, dimensions, and construction lines organised separately?
options: Layers
Sandpaper
T-square handle
Glue tab
questions.correctAnswer: Layers
questions.explanation: Layers group drawing objects by purpose and allow control of visibility, colour, line type, and plotting.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify layers as a CAD organisation tool.

questions.prompt: Which product design term refers to designing for human body size, reach, comfort, and safe use?
options: Ergonomics
Hatching
Foreshortening
Orthocentre
questions.correctAnswer: Ergonomics
questions.explanation: Ergonomics applies human measurements and comfort needs to product design.
questions.learningOutcome: Define ergonomics as a human-centred design consideration.

questions.prompt: Which design process document states the problem, users, constraints, and expected outcome?
options: Design brief
Drawing pin box
Finished receipt
Unlabelled sketch
questions.correctAnswer: Design brief
questions.explanation: A design brief defines the need and conditions that guide the whole design project.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the role of a design brief in product development.

questions.prompt: Which portfolio evidence records how a prototype performed during checks against the specification?
options: Test results and evaluation notes
Blank sheet dividers
A price label only
A copied decoration pattern
questions.correctAnswer: Test results and evaluation notes
questions.explanation: Testing and evaluation evidence shows whether the solution meets the stated requirements.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Identify portfolio evidence used to judge design performance.

questions.prompt: Why should a production drawing avoid placing unnecessary dimensions inside crowded views?
options: It keeps the object outline readable and reduces misinterpretation
It makes the drawing impossible to manufacture
It removes the need for a title block
It changes the material thickness
questions.correctAnswer: It keeps the object outline readable and reduces misinterpretation
questions.explanation: Good dimension placement gives needed sizes without hiding or confusing the object shape.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how dimension placement affects drawing clarity.

questions.prompt: Why is datum dimensioning useful when several holes are located from one straight edge?
options: It reduces accumulated error by measuring each hole from the same reference
It changes every hole into a slot
It removes the need for centre marks
It makes dimensions decorative only
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces accumulated error by measuring each hole from the same reference
questions.explanation: A common datum gives a stable reference so feature positions do not depend on previous measurements.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why datum references improve feature location.

questions.prompt: Why are repeated dimensions normally avoided on a working drawing?
options: They can cause conflict if one copy is changed and another is missed
They make the material stronger
They replace all tolerances
They prove the drawing has no scale
questions.correctAnswer: They can cause conflict if one copy is changed and another is missed
questions.explanation: Each size should usually be stated once in the clearest place to avoid inconsistent instructions.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the risk of redundant dimensions in production drawings.

questions.prompt: Why might a designer specify a tolerance for a hole diameter instead of only a single exact value?
options: Manufacturing has small variations, and the hole still needs to fit its part
A tolerance makes the hole invisible
A tolerance replaces the drawing scale
The hole diameter cannot be measured
questions.correctAnswer: Manufacturing has small variations, and the hole still needs to fit its part
questions.explanation: Tolerances allow realistic variation while protecting function and assembly fit.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why tolerances support fit and function.

questions.prompt: Why does an assembly drawing often include balloons and a parts list?
options: They link each component to its name, material, and quantity
They replace all visible outlines
They turn the assembly into a perspective sketch
They show only the learner's marks
questions.correctAnswer: They link each component to its name, material, and quantity
questions.explanation: Item numbers and a parts list help the maker identify components and assemble them correctly.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how parts lists support assembly communication.

questions.prompt: Why is a half section useful for a symmetrical object such as a turned knob with an internal hole?
options: It can show the outside shape and inside construction in one view
It hides all visible features
It removes the centre line
It changes the object into a flat pattern
questions.correctAnswer: It can show the outside shape and inside construction in one view
questions.explanation: A half section combines an external view on one half with a sectional view on the other.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain when half sections are useful for symmetrical objects.

questions.prompt: Why are adjacent parts in a sectional assembly often hatched at different angles or spacing?
options: To help readers distinguish separate cut components
To show that all parts are made of the same material
To replace the need for outlines
To make dimensions unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: To help readers distinguish separate cut components
questions.explanation: Different hatching patterns separate touching components in a cut view.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain hatching choices used in assembly sections.

questions.prompt: Why is an auxiliary view projected perpendicular to an inclined face?
options: So the inclined face appears in true shape and size
So the title block can be enlarged
So the plan can be erased
So all hidden lines become outlines
questions.correctAnswer: So the inclined face appears in true shape and size
questions.explanation: Projection perpendicular to the sloping surface removes foreshortening for that face.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the geometric purpose of auxiliary projection.

questions.prompt: Why does a circle on an isometric face usually appear as an ellipse?
options: The circular face is viewed at an angle in the isometric plane
The compass cannot draw a circle
The circle is always hidden
The scale automatically doubles the diameter
questions.correctAnswer: The circular face is viewed at an angle in the isometric plane
questions.explanation: A circle on an inclined isometric plane is represented by an ellipse because of the viewing angle.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why circular features become ellipses in isometric drawing.

questions.prompt: Why is cabinet oblique often preferred to cavalier oblique for long objects?
options: It uses reduced depth to lessen visual distortion
It removes the front face
It changes the drawing into a section
It makes every line vertical
questions.correctAnswer: It uses reduced depth to lessen visual distortion
questions.explanation: Cabinet oblique commonly draws depth at half size, making deep objects look more natural.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare cabinet and cavalier oblique projection.

questions.prompt: Why should a presentation rendering show the intended material texture as well as the shape?
options: Material appearance helps viewers understand finish, use, and product character
Texture replaces all dimensions
Texture proves the object has no hidden parts
Texture makes the title block unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Material appearance helps viewers understand finish, use, and product character
questions.explanation: Rendering communicates surface qualities such as wood grain, metal shine, fabric, or plastic finish.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why rendering communicates material qualities.

questions.prompt: Why does the development of a closed cylinder need a rectangle and two circles?
options: The rectangle forms the curved surface, and the circles form the ends
The circles are waste pieces, and the rectangle is the title block
The rectangle forms only fold tabs
The circles replace all dimensions
questions.correctAnswer: The rectangle forms the curved surface, and the circles form the ends
questions.explanation: Opening a cylinder's curved surface produces a rectangle, while its flat ends remain circular.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the parts of a cylinder development.

questions.prompt: Why is a glue tab added to many carton developments?
options: It provides an overlap for joining panels securely
It marks the centre of a circle
It shows the horizon line
It replaces the product label
questions.correctAnswer: It provides an overlap for joining panels securely
questions.explanation: A glue tab gives extra material for bonding one panel to another after folding.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the function of glue tabs in package nets.

questions.prompt: Why should cut lines and fold lines be shown differently on a package net?
options: The maker must know which edges to cut through and which lines to bend
Both line types should always be erased before production
Different lines make the package waterproof
The net cannot be dimensioned otherwise
questions.correctAnswer: The maker must know which edges to cut through and which lines to bend
questions.explanation: Clear line conventions prevent cutting where a fold is required or folding where material should be removed.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain line conventions used in packaging developments.

questions.prompt: Why are object snaps useful when drawing in CAD?
options: They locate exact points such as endpoints, centres, and intersections
They polish the computer screen
They choose material cost automatically
They delete all construction geometry
questions.correctAnswer: They locate exact points such as endpoints, centres, and intersections
questions.explanation: Object snaps improve accuracy by locking the cursor to precise geometric points.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how CAD object snaps improve drawing precision.

questions.prompt: Why should CAD drawings use consistent units from the start of a project?
options: Consistent units prevent scale errors in dimensions, models, and plotted output
Units make every line the same colour
Units remove the need for layers
Units automatically test the prototype
questions.correctAnswer: Consistent units prevent scale errors in dimensions, models, and plotted output
questions.explanation: A clear unit setup keeps geometry, annotation, and printing aligned with the intended real size.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why unit settings matter in digital drawing.

questions.prompt: Why is parametric modelling useful when a design size may need revision?
options: Changing a defined dimension can update related geometry consistently
It prevents any revision after saving
It makes all models flat
It removes the need to understand function
questions.correctAnswer: Changing a defined dimension can update related geometry consistently
questions.explanation: Parametric models use dimensions and relationships so controlled edits can propagate through the design.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the advantage of parametric relationships in digital modelling.

questions.prompt: Why should material choice consider the product's environment of use?
options: Temperature, moisture, wear, and handling can affect performance and safety
Environment only affects the title block
Material choice is unrelated to function
All materials behave the same outdoors
questions.correctAnswer: Temperature, moisture, wear, and handling can affect performance and safety
questions.explanation: A suitable material must withstand expected conditions during normal use.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why operating conditions guide material selection.

questions.prompt: Why is a rounded edge often safer than a sharp corner on a handled product?
options: It reduces the chance of cuts, pressure discomfort, and snagging
It makes the product invisible
It removes the need for testing
It changes plastic into metal
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces the chance of cuts, pressure discomfort, and snagging
questions.explanation: Rounded edges improve touch comfort and reduce hazards during normal handling.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how edge treatment affects safe product use.

questions.prompt: Why does design for maintenance support sustainability?
options: Repairable products can last longer and create less waste
Maintenance makes products disposable
Maintenance replaces user research
Repairability only changes colour
questions.correctAnswer: Repairable products can last longer and create less waste
questions.explanation: Designing for maintenance extends product life and reduces the need for replacement.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how maintainability contributes to sustainable product design.

questions.prompt: Why should user research come before finalising a product specification?
options: It provides evidence of real needs, constraints, and preferences
It is only needed after mass production
It replaces all technical drawings
It makes every prototype successful
questions.correctAnswer: It provides evidence of real needs, constraints, and preferences
questions.explanation: Research helps a designer write requirements that respond to actual users and contexts.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of user research in forming a specification.

questions.prompt: Why is it useful to generate several design concepts before selecting one?
options: It allows comparison of different ways to meet the same need
It guarantees that the first idea is best
It removes the need for evaluation
It prevents feedback from users
questions.correctAnswer: It allows comparison of different ways to meet the same need
questions.explanation: Alternative concepts help the designer judge trade-offs before investing in detailed development.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why designers develop alternative concepts.

questions.prompt: Why should a design specification use measurable criteria where possible?
options: Measurable criteria make testing and evaluation more objective
They stop the designer from sketching
They replace all material notes
They make the product cost-free
questions.correctAnswer: Measurable criteria make testing and evaluation more objective
questions.explanation: Criteria such as size, load, cost, and safety limits can be checked against evidence.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of measurable criteria in a specification.

questions.prompt: Why is a prototype tested before final production?
options: To find weaknesses and improve the design before more resources are used
To avoid documenting the design process
To prove user feedback is unnecessary
To replace all working drawings permanently
questions.correctAnswer: To find weaknesses and improve the design before more resources are used
questions.explanation: Prototype testing provides evidence for refinement before committing to final production.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of prototype testing in iterative design.

questions.prompt: Why should a final portfolio include both successful and unsuccessful design trials?
options: They show the reasoning and evidence behind improvements
They make the portfolio shorter
They remove the need for a final solution
They hide the design process
questions.correctAnswer: They show the reasoning and evidence behind improvements
questions.explanation: Documented trials explain how decisions were made and why the final design changed.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why process evidence strengthens a design portfolio.

questions.prompt: A bracket is 120 mm long on a drawing at scale 1:2. What is the actual bracket length?
options: 240 mm
60 mm
122 mm
118 mm
questions.correctAnswer: 240 mm
questions.explanation: At 1:2 scale, one drawing unit represents two actual units, so 120 mm represents 240 mm.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Apply reduction scale ratios to find actual product sizes.

questions.prompt: A 600 mm tabletop must be drawn at scale 1:5. What length should be shown on the drawing?
options: 120 mm
300 mm
605 mm
questions.correctAnswer: 120 mm
questions.explanation: A 1:5 scale divides actual length by 5, so 600 mm becomes 120 mm on the drawing.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Apply scale ratios when preparing technical drawings.

questions.prompt: A hole is specified as diameter 10 mm plus or minus 0.2 mm. Which measured diameter is within tolerance?
options: 9.9 mm
9.6 mm
questions.correctAnswer: 9.9 mm
questions.explanation: The acceptable range is 9.8 mm to 10.2 mm, so 9.9 mm is within tolerance.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Apply tolerance limits to judge acceptable manufactured sizes.

questions.prompt: A base plate has three holes located 20 mm, 50 mm, and 90 mm from the left edge. Which dimensioning method best reduces cumulative error?
options: Datum dimensions from the left edge to each hole centre
Chain dimensions from one hole to the next only
Unlabelled arrows between random points
Repeating the total length on every view
questions.correctAnswer: Datum dimensions from the left edge to each hole centre
questions.explanation: Using one datum edge gives each hole an independent reference and reduces accumulated position error.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Apply datum dimensioning to locate repeated features.

questions.prompt: A workshop drawing for a small table includes a top, four legs, screws, and corner brackets. Which added item would best help assembly?
options: A numbered parts list matching item balloons on the drawing
A second unrelated title block
A shaded landscape background
A note saying the table looks neat
questions.correctAnswer: A numbered parts list matching item balloons on the drawing
questions.explanation: A linked parts list helps the maker identify each component, quantity, and material during assembly.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Apply assembly documentation conventions to a product drawing.

questions.prompt: A component has a sloping top face with a circular hole drilled square to that face. Which view should be added to show the hole shape accurately?
options: Auxiliary view parallel to the sloping face
Extra title block view
Random oblique sketch
Plan view with all lines erased
questions.correctAnswer: Auxiliary view parallel to the sloping face
questions.explanation: An auxiliary view aligned with the inclined face shows features on that face in true shape.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply auxiliary projection to represent inclined-face features.

questions.prompt: A solid block has a deep rectangular internal slot that is hard to understand from hidden lines. Which drawing choice is most suitable?
options: Use a sectional view through the slot
Remove all views except the plan
Use only a colour rendering
Hide the slot because it is internal
questions.correctAnswer: Use a sectional view through the slot
questions.explanation: A section through the slot reveals its internal shape directly and reduces hidden-line clutter.
questions.learningOutcome: Select a sectional view to clarify internal details.

questions.prompt: A symmetrical pulley needs to show its outside profile and the shape of its central bore in one view. Which section is most efficient?
options: Half section
Removed plan only
Exploded perspective only
Blank elevation
questions.correctAnswer: Half section
questions.explanation: A half section is efficient for symmetrical objects because it combines external and internal information.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose a sectional method for a symmetrical component.

questions.prompt: A first-angle drawing has a front view and needs a right-side view. Where is the right-side view normally placed?
options: To the left of the front view
To the right of the front view
Above the front view
Inside the front view
questions.correctAnswer: To the left of the front view
questions.explanation: In first-angle projection, side views are placed opposite the side from which the object is viewed.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply first-angle view placement conventions.

questions.prompt: A cuboid has length 80 mm, width 50 mm, and height 30 mm. Which dimensions are shown in the plan view?
options: Length and width
Width and height
Length and height
Diameter and radius only
questions.correctAnswer: Length and width
questions.explanation: The plan is viewed from above, so it shows the top outline with length and width.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply view-direction reasoning to identify dimensions shown in orthographic views.

questions.prompt: A product has a large flat front face that must remain true shape in a pictorial drawing. Which method is most suitable?
options: Oblique drawing
Sectional elevation
Orthographic plan only
Dimension table only
questions.correctAnswer: Oblique drawing
questions.explanation: Oblique drawing keeps the front face in true shape while projecting depth backwards.
questions.learningOutcome: Select pictorial methods for communicating product features.

questions.prompt: A designer wants to show a product as users would see it at eye level in a room. Which drawing method is most appropriate?
options: Perspective drawing
First-angle symbol only
Chain dimensioning
Surface hatching
questions.correctAnswer: Perspective drawing
questions.explanation: Perspective drawing gives a realistic visual impression based on eye level and vanishing points.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply perspective drawing to user-facing product presentation.

questions.prompt: A metal kettle handle is rendered with sharp white highlights, dark reflected edges, and smooth grey tones. What material quality is being communicated?
options: Shiny metal surface
Transparent glass sheet
Rough untreated timber
Soft woven fabric
questions.correctAnswer: Shiny metal surface
questions.explanation: High contrast highlights and reflected edges commonly suggest polished or shiny metal.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply rendering cues to communicate material appearance.

questions.prompt: A poster stand design must communicate both final appearance and key construction details to a review panel. Which presentation set is strongest?
options: Rendered pictorial view plus dimensioned orthographic views
Only a colourful border pattern
Only a parts price list
Only unlabelled construction lines
questions.correctAnswer: Rendered pictorial view plus dimensioned orthographic views
questions.explanation: The rendered view communicates appearance, while orthographic views communicate accurate construction information.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply mixed drawing types for product presentation and production.

questions.prompt: A cylindrical container has diameter 70 mm. Using 3.142 for circumference, what is the approximate length of the curved-surface development?
options: 220 mm
140 mm
70 mm
490 mm
questions.correctAnswer: 220 mm
questions.explanation: The length is the circumference, about 3.142 x 70 mm = 219.94 mm, which rounds to 220 mm.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply circumference calculation to cylindrical developments.

questions.prompt: A rectangular carton is 120 mm long, 60 mm wide, and 80 mm high. Which panels must appear in a simple net?
options: Top, bottom, two long sides, two short sides, and a joining tab
Only one front rectangle
Only two circles and a title block
Only hidden lines and no panels
questions.correctAnswer: Top, bottom, two long sides, two short sides, and a joining tab
questions.explanation: A closed rectangular carton needs all six faces and a practical joining allowance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply net planning to a rectangular package.

questions.prompt: A folded card stand keeps collapsing along a fold. Which development improvement is most relevant?
options: Add locking tabs or triangular support folds at the weak area
Delete all fold lines
Make the title block larger
Use only a front elevation
questions.correctAnswer: Add locking tabs or triangular support folds at the weak area
questions.explanation: Structural folds or tabs can stiffen the development and help it hold shape after assembly.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply folding and tab features to improve sheet-material structures.

questions.prompt: A CAD drawing needs outlines to print thick and dimensions to print thin. Which setup best supports this?
options: Use separate layers with assigned line weights
Draw everything on one layer with one colour
Export only a screenshot
Turn off all object snaps
questions.correctAnswer: Use separate layers with assigned line weights
questions.explanation: Layer properties can control line weight and plotting style for different drawing information.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply layer properties to organise CAD output.

questions.prompt: A CAD rectangle must remain 2:1 in length-to-width ratio when edited. Which parametric control would help most?
options: A dimensional relationship linking length to twice the width
A random colour fill
A hidden title block
A deleted constraint set
questions.correctAnswer: A dimensional relationship linking length to twice the width
questions.explanation: A parametric relation preserves the intended proportion when one dimension changes.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply parametric relationships to maintain design intent.

questions.prompt: A 3D model of a phone stand needs rounded corners for safe handling. Which digital modelling operation best creates them?
options: Fillet
Explode text
Mirror title block
Freeze layer
questions.correctAnswer: Fillet
questions.explanation: A fillet creates rounded edges or corners with a specified radius.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply common 3D CAD features to product safety and form.

questions.prompt: A product drawing must be shared for review but not easily edited by classmates. Which output format is usually most suitable?
options: PDF
Temporary scratch file
Blank template
Unfinished autosave only
questions.correctAnswer: PDF
questions.explanation: PDF output preserves layout and is widely used for viewing and printing reviewed drawings.
questions.learningOutcome: Select an appropriate digital output for sharing design drawings.

questions.prompt: A school outdoor sign must resist rain and sunlight. Which material choice is most appropriate from the options?
options: Coated metal sheet with protected edges
Untreated soft cardboard
Absorbent tissue layers
Unsealed writing paper
questions.correctAnswer: Coated metal sheet with protected edges
questions.explanation: Coated metal can resist weather better than absorbent paper-based materials when edges are protected.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply material properties to outdoor product requirements.

questions.prompt: A handle will be used by adults and younger learners. Which design action best improves ergonomic fit?
options: Use hand-size data to set a comfortable grip diameter and clearance
Choose a colour before checking grip
Make the handle as sharp as possible
Hide the handle in the title block
questions.correctAnswer: Use hand-size data to set a comfortable grip diameter and clearance
questions.explanation: Ergonomic design uses user measurements and handling needs to set safe, comfortable dimensions.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply human-factor data to product design decisions.

questions.prompt: A product is made from sheet material and produces many offcuts. Which production planning method can reduce waste?
options: Nest part shapes efficiently on the sheet before cutting
Cut every part from the centre only
Ignore the grain or sheet direction in all cases
Increase offcut size deliberately
questions.correctAnswer: Nest part shapes efficiently on the sheet before cutting
questions.explanation: Nesting arranges parts to use sheet area efficiently while respecting required orientation.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply cutting-layout planning to reduce material waste.

questions.prompt: A learner designs a wooden stool for repeated classroom use. Which joint choice is most suitable from the options?
options: Strong mechanical joints reinforced where loads meet
Temporary tape only at every leg
No joint between the seat and legs
Decorative paint used as the only fastening
questions.correctAnswer: Strong mechanical joints reinforced where loads meet
questions.explanation: A load-bearing stool needs joints that transfer forces safely and resist repeated use.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply construction reasoning to load-bearing product design.

questions.prompt: A community notice holder must be low cost, easy to repair locally, and safe for children. Which specification item best captures these needs?
options: Use available materials, replaceable parts, smooth edges, and stable fixing
Use rare imported parts and sharp edges
Allow no maintenance access
Judge success only by bright colour
questions.correctAnswer: Use available materials, replaceable parts, smooth edges, and stable fixing
questions.explanation: The specification should translate cost, repair, and safety needs into testable design requirements.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Apply user needs and constraints to product specifications.

questions.prompt: A prototype phone stand tips over when a large phone is placed on it. Which improvement should be tried first?
options: Widen the base or lower the centre of gravity and retest
Only change the colour
Remove the support surface
Make the title block bigger
questions.correctAnswer: Widen the base or lower the centre of gravity and retest
questions.explanation: Stability problems are addressed by improving support geometry and then checking the change against the load.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Apply prototype test findings to choose design improvements.

questions.prompt: A design brief asks for a portable display stand that fits in a school bag. Which measurable specification best supports the brief?
options: The folded stand shall fit within a 300 mm by 220 mm bag compartment
The stand shall look nice to everyone
The stand shall have an interesting story
The stand shall use any size available
questions.correctAnswer: The folded stand shall fit within a 300 mm by 220 mm bag compartment
questions.explanation: A measurable size requirement makes portability testable and directly linked to the brief.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Apply measurable criteria to convert a brief into a specification.

questions.prompt: A learner compares three storage-rack ideas using cost, strength, safety, and ease of repair. Which tool best supports a fair selection?
options: A weighted decision matrix with evidence for each score
A random vote without criteria
A copied catalogue page only
A list of favourite colours
questions.correctAnswer: A weighted decision matrix with evidence for each score
questions.explanation: A decision matrix helps compare alternatives against agreed criteria and justify selection.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Apply evaluation criteria to select a design concept.

questions.prompt: A final portfolio needs evidence that a design was improved after testing. Which entry is most useful?
options: Before-and-after sketches with test results explaining each change
Only the learner's signature
Only a blank assessment page
Only a decorative cover
questions.correctAnswer: Before-and-after sketches with test results explaining each change
questions.explanation: Clear improvement evidence links test findings to specific design changes.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Apply portfolio documentation methods to show design iteration.

questions.prompt: A dimensioned drawing gives a chain of four small distances and no overall length. What is the main manufacturing risk?
options: Small errors can accumulate and make the final feature positions inaccurate
The drawing will automatically become full size
The material will become waterproof
The title block will print twice
questions.correctAnswer: Small errors can accumulate and make the final feature positions inaccurate
questions.explanation: Chain dimensions can transfer each small measurement error to the next feature unless controlled by datums or checks.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse risks caused by unsuitable dimensioning methods.

questions.prompt: A production drawing states the material as metal but gives no thickness, finish, or grade. What is the strongest criticism?
options: The material specification is too vague for reliable manufacture
The drawing has too many accurate dimensions
The views must all be perspective views
The product cannot have a front view
questions.correctAnswer: The material specification is too vague for reliable manufacture
questions.explanation: Material notes need enough detail for selection, performance, finishing, and cost control.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse completeness of technical specifications on working drawings.

questions.prompt: An assembly drawing shows the final product but no exploded view for hidden fasteners inside the joint. What problem may result?
options: The maker may not understand the order and position of concealed parts
The finished product will have no height
The title block will become a cutting plane
All components will become the same material
questions.correctAnswer: The maker may not understand the order and position of concealed parts
questions.explanation: Exploded views and fastener notes clarify how components fit together, especially where parts are hidden.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse missing assembly information in product documentation.

questions.prompt: A sectional view of a bracket hatches a hollow space as if it were solid material. What is wrong with the drawing?
options: It misrepresents empty space as cut material
It correctly shows that every opening is solid
It only needs a larger border
It should remove every visible outline
questions.correctAnswer: It misrepresents empty space as cut material
questions.explanation: Only material cut by the cutting plane is hatched; holes and voids remain unhatched.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse hatching errors in sectional views.

questions.prompt: A learner draws an auxiliary view but projects it from the horizontal plan instead of from the inclined face. What is the likely result?
options: The inclined surface will still be distorted rather than shown in true shape
The drawing will automatically become a net
The front view will disappear
The material will be selected automatically
questions.correctAnswer: The inclined surface will still be distorted rather than shown in true shape
questions.explanation: An auxiliary view must be projected in the correct direction relative to the inclined surface.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse errors in auxiliary projection setup.

questions.prompt: An orthographic drawing mixes first-angle placement for the plan with third-angle placement for the side view. What is the main issue?
options: The drawing may be interpreted incorrectly because the projection system is inconsistent
The object will have no true dimensions
All views become rendered views
The line weights become impossible to print
questions.correctAnswer: The drawing may be interpreted incorrectly because the projection system is inconsistent
questions.explanation: A single projection system and symbol should be used so readers know how the views relate.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the effect of inconsistent orthographic view placement.

questions.prompt: An isometric drawing of a cube uses one axis at 20 degrees and another at 45 degrees without a design reason. What is the strongest evaluation?
options: The inconsistent axes distort the form and weaken technical communication
The cube is automatically shown in true orthographic views
The drawing becomes a cylinder development
The title block fixes the axis error
questions.correctAnswer: The inconsistent axes distort the form and weaken technical communication
questions.explanation: Isometric drawings depend on consistent axis directions to keep the pictorial form readable.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse common construction errors in isometric drawing.

questions.prompt: A rendered product board looks attractive but gives no scale, material notes, or intended user context. What is the main weakness?
options: It does not provide enough information to judge feasibility and suitability
It has too much manufacturing detail
It proves the product is ready for production
It replaces prototype testing
questions.correctAnswer: It does not provide enough information to judge feasibility and suitability
questions.explanation: Presentation must communicate practical design information as well as visual appeal.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse whether presentation drawings communicate enough design information.

questions.prompt: A two-point perspective sketch of a rectangular kiosk sends some horizontal depth edges to one vanishing point and some parallel depth edges to another unrelated point. What error does this create?
options: Parallel receding edges no longer appear to belong to the same form
The drawing gains exact manufacturing dimensions
The horizon line becomes unnecessary
The kiosk becomes a sectional drawing
questions.correctAnswer: Parallel receding edges no longer appear to belong to the same form
questions.explanation: In perspective, each set of parallel receding edges should converge consistently to its vanishing point.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse perspective construction errors in product sketches.

questions.prompt: A package net has correct panels but no allowance for material thickness at tight folds. What production issue may appear?
options: The assembled package may fit poorly or bulge at the folds
The printed colours will become invisible
The package will require no cutting
The net will automatically become circular
questions.correctAnswer: The assembled package may fit poorly or bulge at the folds
questions.explanation: Thicker materials need fold allowances or adjusted dimensions so the final package fits properly.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how material thickness affects package development.

questions.prompt: A cylindrical label development is calculated from diameter but leaves no overlap for adhesive. What is the likely weakness?
options: The label may not join securely around the container
The diameter will become zero
The label will automatically show a lid
The drawing scale will be impossible to state
questions.correctAnswer: The label may not join securely around the container
questions.explanation: A wraparound label usually needs an added overlap beyond circumference for bonding.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse joining requirements in surface developments.

questions.prompt: A folded display stand uses very thin card for a heavy object and fails during testing. Which conclusion is most defensible?
options: The material and structural form do not meet the load requirement
The stand failed only because it had a title block
Thin card is always suitable for any load
Testing should be ignored because the sketch was neat
questions.correctAnswer: The material and structural form do not meet the load requirement
questions.explanation: Test failure shows that both material strength and structural design must be reconsidered.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse performance failures in sheet-material structures.

questions.prompt: A CAD file has all geometry, dimensions, construction lines, and hatching on one unlocked layer. What is the main workflow risk?
options: Important elements are harder to hide, protect, edit, and plot correctly
The file cannot contain straight lines
The computer will choose the material automatically
All dimensions become tolerances
questions.correctAnswer: Important elements are harder to hide, protect, edit, and plot correctly
questions.explanation: Poor layer organisation slows editing and increases the chance of printing or modifying the wrong elements.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the impact of poor CAD file organisation.

questions.prompt: A CAD model is edited by dragging faces, and old dimensions are left unchanged in the drawing sheet. What risk is introduced?
options: The documented dimensions may no longer match the model geometry
The model becomes impossible to save as a file
Every layer becomes a material texture
The drawing automatically becomes first-angle
questions.correctAnswer: The documented dimensions may no longer match the model geometry
questions.explanation: After geometry changes, dimensions and annotations must be regenerated or checked against the updated model.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse why CAD documentation must be checked after edits.

questions.prompt: A product team shares a file named final_final2 without dates, revision notes, or author details. What professional problem does this create?
options: The team may not know which version is approved or what changed
The file name makes the design stronger
The drawing will print with perfect scale
The file cannot contain any dimensions
questions.correctAnswer: The team may not know which version is approved or what changed
questions.explanation: Clear version control records help teams track approved changes and avoid using outdated information.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse risks caused by weak digital file control.

questions.prompt: A chair design uses attractive curves but places the seat too high for its intended learners. Which design factor has been neglected most?
options: Ergonomic fit for the user group
Line weight variation only
Decorative border spacing
The number of portfolio pages
questions.correctAnswer: Ergonomic fit for the user group
questions.explanation: A product that does not fit the user's body measurements is weak even if it looks attractive.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse product decisions using ergonomic criteria.

questions.prompt: A recycled plastic is available locally but cracks during normal load testing. Which conclusion best balances sustainability and performance?
options: It is unsuitable unless redesigned or blended to meet safety requirements
It should be used because recycled material is always sufficient
Testing should stop because the material is local
Cracking is acceptable if the colour is attractive
questions.correctAnswer: It is unsuitable unless redesigned or blended to meet safety requirements
questions.explanation: Sustainable material choices must still meet functional and safety requirements.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse trade-offs between sustainability and material performance.

questions.prompt: A product is glued permanently shut even though a part inside is likely to wear out. What sustainability issue is strongest?
options: Poor repair access may shorten the product's useful life
Permanent glue always improves maintainability
Wear parts should never be considered
Repair access only affects drawing colour
questions.correctAnswer: Poor repair access may shorten the product's useful life
questions.explanation: Design for repair considers access to parts that may need maintenance or replacement.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse maintainability as part of sustainable product design.

questions.prompt: A learner chooses the cheapest material for a school display product, but it splinters and leaves sharp edges after cutting. Which criterion was underweighted?
options: User safety and finish quality
Sheet border thickness only
Colour naming style
Number of CAD commands memorised
questions.correctAnswer: User safety and finish quality
questions.explanation: Cost is important, but materials must also be safe to make, finish, and use.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse material choices using safety and quality criteria.

questions.prompt: A portfolio has final drawings and a finished model but no brief, research, specification, concept comparison, or test evidence. What is the main limitation?
options: It does not show how design decisions were justified
It proves the process was fully documented
It makes the model more durable
It removes the need for evaluation
questions.correctAnswer: It does not show how design decisions were justified
questions.explanation: A strong portfolio documents the reasoning, evidence, and iteration behind the final outcome.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the completeness of design portfolio evidence.

questions.prompt: A rural clinic needs a low-cost medicine shelf that is easy to clean, secure, and repair using local skills. Which design strategy is strongest?
options: Use washable surfaces, lockable simple joinery, replaceable parts, and locally available materials
Use absorbent untreated board with no door
Use sealed imported parts that cannot be repaired
Focus only on decorative patterns and ignore cleaning
questions.correctAnswer: Use washable surfaces, lockable simple joinery, replaceable parts, and locally available materials
questions.explanation: The strongest strategy balances hygiene, security, maintainability, cost, and local production capacity.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Create a design strategy that balances user needs, context, material, and maintenance.

questions.prompt: A complex casing has an inclined control panel, internal ribs, screw bosses, and a removable cover. Which drawing package would communicate it best for manufacture?
options: Orthographic views, auxiliary view for the panel, sectional view through ribs, exploded assembly, dimensions, tolerances, and material notes
Only one shaded perspective sketch with no sizes
Only a title block and school name
Only a list of colours and decorative patterns
questions.correctAnswer: Orthographic views, auxiliary view for the panel, sectional view through ribs, exploded assembly, dimensions, tolerances, and material notes
questions.explanation: Complex products need a coordinated set of views and specifications to show external form, internal detail, assembly, and production requirements.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Create a complete drawing package for a multi-feature product.

questions.prompt: A learner must design a package for fragile handmade soap bars sold at a school exhibition. Which development plan is most complete?
options: A dimensioned net with fold lines, cut lines, glue tab, protective insert, label area, material thickness allowance, and efficient sheet layout
A single coloured rectangle with no folds
A cylindrical label for a box shape only
Only a photograph of another package
questions.correctAnswer: A dimensioned net with fold lines, cut lines, glue tab, protective insert, label area, material thickness allowance, and efficient sheet layout
questions.explanation: The plan addresses forming, joining, protection, communication, material behaviour, and waste reduction.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a package development that satisfies protection, branding, and production requirements.

questions.prompt: A CAD team is preparing a shared template for senior-school design projects. Which setup is most professional?
options: Standard units, sheet sizes, title block, named layers, dimension styles, text styles, revision table, and plotting presets
One blank file with no units and every object on layer zero
A screenshot folder with no drawing files
A file named final with no backup or title information
questions.correctAnswer: Standard units, sheet sizes, title block, named layers, dimension styles, text styles, revision table, and plotting presets
questions.explanation: A template improves consistency, accuracy, collaboration, revision tracking, and reliable output.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a CAD setup that supports collaboration and production documentation.

questions.prompt: A school wants twenty identical stools with low material waste and consistent quality. Which production plan is best?
options: Prepare jigs, a nested cutting layout, checked dimensions, repeatable joints, and quality checks after assembly
Cut each part by guessing from a rough sketch
Make every stool a different size without records
Paint first and decide dimensions later
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare jigs, a nested cutting layout, checked dimensions, repeatable joints, and quality checks after assembly
questions.explanation: Repeat production needs controlled cutting, accurate fixtures, consistent joining, and inspection.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a production plan for repeatable, material-efficient manufacture.

questions.prompt: A portable laptop stand must be stable, fold flat, avoid scratching the laptop, and use minimal sheet material. Which concept best balances these requirements?
options: Interlocking folded panels with wide support stance, soft contact pads, locking slots, and nested part layout
A tall narrow stand with sharp bare edges
A solid block that cannot fold and wastes material
A decorative poster with no support function
questions.correctAnswer: Interlocking folded panels with wide support stance, soft contact pads, locking slots, and nested part layout
questions.explanation: The concept integrates stability, portability, surface protection, locking, and material efficiency.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Create an integrated product concept from multiple performance criteria.

questions.prompt: A design panel includes users, teachers, and a local maker. Which presentation sequence would communicate the project most effectively?
options: State the need, summarise research, show criteria, compare concepts, explain selected drawings and materials, present test evidence, then justify improvements
Begin with unrelated decoration and end before showing the product
Read only the parts list without explaining the problem
Show final colours and avoid questions about testing
questions.correctAnswer: State the need, summarise research, show criteria, compare concepts, explain selected drawings and materials, present test evidence, then justify improvements
questions.explanation: A clear sequence helps different audiences understand the problem, evidence, solution, and refinement.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a logical presentation structure for defending a design project.

questions.prompt: A market-stall display must pack flat, assemble without tools, resist wind, and show prices clearly. Which documentation set best guides production and use?
options: Dimensioned development, assembly sequence, locking-tab details, material notes, stability test notes, and labelled presentation view
Only a rendered front view with no sizes
Only a receipt for materials
Only a colour swatch without construction details
questions.correctAnswer: Dimensioned development, assembly sequence, locking-tab details, material notes, stability test notes, and labelled presentation view
questions.explanation: The documentation covers manufacture, folding, assembly, stability, materials, and user-facing communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Create documentation for a foldable product with performance and presentation needs.

questions.prompt: A product must be assembled by another learner without verbal help. Which drawing set best supports independent assembly?
options: Exploded view, final assembly view, item balloons, parts list, fastener sizes, orientation marks, and brief assembly notes
Only a final photograph with no labels
Only material samples in a box
Only the designer's name and date
questions.correctAnswer: Exploded view, final assembly view, item balloons, parts list, fastener sizes, orientation marks, and brief assembly notes
questions.explanation: Independent assembly needs part identification, relationships, quantities, orientation, and fastening guidance.
questions.strandTitle: Technical Drawing Standards and Working Drawings
questions.learningOutcome: Create a complete assembly communication set for another maker.

questions.prompt: A final Grade 12 design portfolio must prove a complete, evidence-based process. Which evidence set is strongest?
options: Brief, research, specification, concept sketches, selection matrix, development drawings, CAD or working drawings, prototype tests, evaluation, and justified improvements
Only a final product photograph and learner name
Only copied internet images without acknowledgement
Only a parts list with no design decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Brief, research, specification, concept sketches, selection matrix, development drawings, CAD or working drawings, prototype tests, evaluation, and justified improvements
questions.explanation: A complete portfolio records the need, evidence, decisions, technical communication, testing, and refinement behind the final product.
questions.strandTitle: Product Design Process and Portfolio Practice
questions.learningOutcome: Create a complete evidence structure for a senior-school design portfolio.
